rationale:
The selected theorem is not atomic. Its supplied proof has two independent, reusable halves, and they need different tools.

**Children.**
(A) `regcomp_covector_sq_sum_basis_invariant` is step 2: Σ_j α(b∘j)² does not depend on the orthonormal basis b. Its tools are orthonormal expansion, multilinearity and Parseval.
(B) `regcomp_covector_sq_sum_basisFun` is steps 1 and 3–6: for the standard basis e, Σ_j α(e∘j)² = n!·|α|_E². Its tools are tied to the definition of covectorEuclideanNorm: vanishing on repeated arguments, the sign under permutations, the (increasing tuple, permutation) ↔ injective tuple bijection via Tuple.sort and StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT, and |Perm(Fin n)| = n!.

**Assembly.** The selected statement is step 7: instantiate A with (b, b') := (f, EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ) and conclude with B. In Lean:
`intro P n α f; rw [Submission.regcomp_covector_sq_sum_basis_invariant P n α f (EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ)]; exact Submission.regcomp_covector_sq_sum_basisFun P n α`.
A and B do not depend on each other, so they can be formalized in parallel and a failure in one stays isolated.

**Verification.**
(i) Both frozen child types elaborate after `import GMT.Ch07.Submission` in the contract's namespace and opens.
(ii) With both children as sorry stubs, the selected frozen type is proved by this assembly. `#print axioms` shows propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound, plus sorryAx from the stubs. An independent reviewer subagent re-checked this in its own scratch file. It also checked the converse, that each child follows from the selected statement, so neither child over-claims.
(iii) A complete Lean prototype (/tmp/cvsq-split/Full.lean) proves A (about 60 lines), B (about 60 lines) and the selected statement. All three use only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound. The reviewer re-ran it and got the same result.
(iv) The cases n = 0, P = 0 and n > P are covered by the general arguments.

**Not circular, no overlap.** B is a strict special case of the selected statement (f = e), not a restatement: the general f still needs A. Neither child has the same type as any other DAG node; the accepted covectorEuclideanNorm_gram_bounds and the siblings all have different types. Neither name occurs in dag.json, nodes/, 514 git refs or 117 worktree Submission.lean files.

**Reviewer.** The verdict was ACCEPT. Its only reservation was that keeping the node atomic would also be sound and cheaper in pipeline overhead. I kept the split for isolation and reusability. I applied its optional wording fixes to B: define |α|_E, cite nsmul_eq_mul, and clarify the n > P case.

**Sources consulted.** Simon Ch. 6, 1.2 and 1.5 (book/chapter-06.txt lines 43–47 and 94–97): coefficients α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n}) for increasing indices, with {dx^I} orthonormal. Public source: https://www.mathphysicsbook.com/mathematics/vector-algebras/exterior-forms/exterior-forms-as-anti-symmetric-arrays/ ⟨φ,ψ⟩ = (1/k!)·(full-index contraction), consistent with B's n! normalisation.

subproblems.title: Orthonormal-basis invariance of the full squared-tuple sum Σ_j α(b∘j)²
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P (α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n, a continuous alternating n-linear form on ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)), and let b = (b_0, …, b_{P−1}) and b' = (b'_0, …, b'_{P−1}) be orthonormal bases of ℝ^P indexed by Fin P. Then Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(b_{j(0)}, …, b_{j(n−1)})² = Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(b'_{j(0)}, …, b'_{j(n−1)})².
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n) (b b' : OrthonormalBasis (Fin P) ℝ (Euclid P)), ∑ j : Fin n → Fin P, (α (fun k => b (j k))) ^ 2 = ∑ j : Fin n → Fin P, (α (fun k => b' (j k))) ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 2 of the parent node's supplied proof (basis independence of S_b(α) := Σ_j α(b∘j)²), in the “equivalent implementation” recorded there: expand every slot in an orthonormal basis by multilinearity and use Σ_i ⟨x, b_i⟩⟨b_i, y⟩ = ⟨x, y⟩ (OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner) in each of the n slots, so that all cross terms cancel. Here b is expanded directly in b' (instead of expanding both bases in the standard basis e), which proves the two-basis statement in one pass. Only the multilinearity of α is used.

Notation. ℝ^P = Euclid P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P) with the real inner product ⟨·,·⟩. For a family v : Fin P → ℝ^P and a : Fin n → Fin P write v∘a := (v_{a(0)}, …, v_{a(n−1)}) (in Lean: fun k => v (a k)). Sums over j, a, a' range over the finite type Fin n → Fin P, sums over i, s, t range over Fin P, and products over k range over Fin n. For i, s ∈ Fin P put c(i, s) := ⟨b'_s, b_i⟩ ∈ ℝ. Write S_b := Σ_j α(b∘j)² and S_{b'} := Σ_j α(b'∘j)². We must show S_b = S_{b'}.

1. (Expansion of b in b'.) Since b' is an orthonormal basis, x = Σ_s ⟨b'_s, x⟩ b'_s for every x ∈ ℝ^P (OrthonormalBasis.sum_repr'). Taking x = b_i gives b_i = Σ_s c(i, s) b'_s for every i ∈ Fin P.

2. (Multilinear expansion.) Fix j : Fin n → Fin P. By step 1 the k-th argument of α(b∘j) is b_{j(k)} = Σ_s c(j(k), s) b'_s. Since α is linear in each of its n arguments, expanding all n slots produces one summand for every choice a : Fin n → Fin P of an index a(k) in each slot k (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_sum), and pulling the scalars out of all slots (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ) gives
   α(b∘j) = Σ_a (Π_k c(j(k), a(k))) · α(b'∘a).

3. (Square and sum.) For each j, squaring step 2 and using (Σ_a x_a)(Σ_{a'} y_{a'}) = Σ_a Σ_{a'} x_a y_{a'} (Finset.sum_mul_sum) gives
   α(b∘j)² = Σ_a Σ_{a'} (Π_k c(j(k), a(k))) α(b'∘a) · (Π_k c(j(k), a'(k))) α(b'∘a').
   Summing over j, moving the finite sum over j inside the sums over a and a' (Finset.sum_comm) and using Π_k x_k · Π_k y_k = Π_k x_k y_k (Finset.prod_mul_distrib),
   S_b = Σ_a Σ_{a'} α(b'∘a) α(b'∘a') · T(a, a'),   where T(a, a') := Σ_j Π_k c(j(k), a(k)) c(j(k), a'(k)).

4. (Factorisation of T.) For fixed a, a' the k-th factor of the product depends on j only through j(k). By distributivity, a product over k ∈ Fin n of sums over i ∈ Fin P is the sum over all j : Fin n → Fin P of the products of the selected terms (Fintype.prod_sum: Π_k Σ_i g(k, i) = Σ_j Π_k g(k, j(k))). With g(k, i) := c(i, a(k)) c(i, a'(k)) this gives
   T(a, a') = Π_k Σ_i c(i, a(k)) c(i, a'(k)).

5. (Parseval for b; orthonormality of b'.) For s, t ∈ Fin P, symmetry of the real inner product gives c(i, s) c(i, t) = ⟨b'_s, b_i⟩⟨b_i, b'_t⟩, hence Σ_i c(i, s) c(i, t) = Σ_i ⟨b'_s, b_i⟩⟨b_i, b'_t⟩ = ⟨b'_s, b'_t⟩ (OrthonormalBasis.sum_inner_mul_inner for the orthonormal basis b), and ⟨b'_s, b'_t⟩ = 1 if s = t and 0 otherwise because b' is orthonormal (orthonormal_iff_ite). By step 4, T(a, a') = Π_k [a(k) = a'(k)]. If a' = a every factor is 1, so T(a, a) = 1; if a' ≠ a there is k with a(k) ≠ a'(k), that factor is 0, and T(a, a') = 0.

6. (Conclusion.) Substituting step 5 into step 3, for each a only the term a' = a of the inner sum survives (Finset.sum_eq_single), so S_b = Σ_a α(b'∘a) · α(b'∘a) = Σ_a α(b'∘a)² = S_{b'}. ∎

Degenerate cases need no separate treatment: for n = 0 the type Fin 0 → Fin P has exactly one element and every product over k is empty (= 1), so the steps hold verbatim and both sides equal α(empty tuple)²; for P = 0 and n ≥ 1 all sums over j, a, a' are empty and both sides are 0.

Lean remark: when a sum such as Σ_j α(b∘j)² opens a calc chain, write its binder with an explicit type (∑ j : Fin n → Fin P, …); an unannotated binder there made elaboration time out in a prototype of this proof.
proof_key_steps: Expand b_i = Σ_s ⟨b'_s, b_i⟩ b'_s and use multilinearity: α(b∘j) = Σ_a (Π_k c(j(k), a(k)))·α(b'∘a) with c(i, s) = ⟨b'_s, b_i⟩.
Square, sum over j and interchange the finite sums: S_b = Σ_a Σ_{a'} α(b'∘a) α(b'∘a') · Σ_j Π_k c(j(k), a(k)) c(j(k), a'(k)).
Factor the j-sum as Π_k Σ_i c(i, a(k)) c(i, a'(k)) and evaluate each factor as δ_{a(k), a'(k)} by Parseval for b and orthonormality of b'.
Only a' = a survives, so S_b = Σ_a α(b'∘a)² = S_{b'}.

subproblems.title: Standard-basis normalisation: Σ_j α(e∘j)² = n!·|α|_E²
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let α be an n-covector on ℝ^P (α ∈ Covector (Euclid P) n, a continuous alternating n-linear form on ℝ^P = EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin P)), and let e_i = EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i (i ∈ Fin P) be the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P. Then Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(e_{j(0)}, …, e_{j(n−1)})² = n!·|α|_E², where |α|_E = covectorEuclideanNorm α = (Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P strictly increasing} α(e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)})²)^{1/2}.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (α : Covector (Euclid P) n), ∑ j : Fin n → Fin P, (α (fun k => EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ (j k))) ^ 2 = (n.factorial : ℝ) * covectorEuclideanNorm α ^ 2
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 1 and 3–6 of the parent node's supplied proof (the standard-basis computation S_e(α) = n!·|α|_E²); the coefficients α(e∘I), I strictly increasing, are Simon's α_{i_1…i_n} = α(e_{i_1}, …, e_{i_n}) of Ch. 6, 1.2 (chapter-06.txt lines 43–47), which are orthonormal coordinates by 1.5 (lines 94–97).

Notation. e_i := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin P) ℝ i is the standard orthonormal basis of ℝ^P = Euclid P, and |α|_E := covectorEuclideanNorm α. For I : Fin n → Fin P write e∘I := (e_{I(0)}, …, e_{I(n−1)}) (in Lean: fun k => e (I k)). Perm(Fin n) is the group of permutations of Fin n; it has n! elements (Fintype.card_perm, Fintype.card_fin). Let A := {I : Fin n → Fin P | I strictly increasing (StrictMono I)} and Inj := {j : Fin n → Fin P | j injective}.

1. (Square of the norm.) By definition |α|_E = √N with N := Σ_{I : Fin n → Fin P} (if I ∈ A then α(e∘I)² else 0). Every summand is ≥ 0, so N ≥ 0 and |α|_E² = N (Real.sq_sqrt). Multiplying by n!, distributing (Finset.mul_sum) and writing n!·x = Σ_{π ∈ Perm(Fin n)} x (Finset.sum_const, nsmul_eq_mul and |Perm(Fin n)| = n!),
   n!·|α|_E² = Σ_{I ∈ A} Σ_{π ∈ Perm(Fin n)} α(e∘I)² = Σ_{(I, π) ∈ A × Perm(Fin n)} α(e∘I)².

2. (Non-injective tuples contribute 0.) Let j : Fin n → Fin P be non-injective: there are k ≠ k' with j(k) = j(k'). Then the k-th and k'-th entries e_{j(k)} = e_{j(k')} of e∘j coincide, so the n-tuple e∘j is not injective, and α(e∘j) = 0 because α is alternating (ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_eq_zero_of_not_injective). Therefore Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(e∘j)² = Σ_{j ∈ Inj} α(e∘j)² (Finset.sum_filter_of_ne).

3. (Permuting slots only changes the sign.) For I : Fin n → Fin P and π ∈ Perm(Fin n) we have e∘(I∘π) = (e∘I)∘π, so α(e∘(I∘π)) = sign(π)·α(e∘I) (AlternatingMap.map_perm applied to α.toAlternatingMap). Since sign(π) ∈ {1, −1} (Int.units_eq_one_or), α(e∘(I∘π))² = α(e∘I)².

4. (Increasing tuples × permutations ≅ injective tuples.) Define Φ : A × Perm(Fin n) → Inj by Φ(I, π) := I∘π.
   (a) Φ lands in Inj: a strictly increasing I is injective (StrictMono.injective) and π is a bijection, so I∘π is injective.
   (b) Φ is injective: suppose I∘π = I'∘π' with I, I' ∈ A. Since π and π' are surjective, range(I) = range(I∘π) = range(I'∘π') = range(I') (EquivLike.range_comp). Two strictly increasing maps from the well-ordered Fin n into Fin P with the same range are equal (StrictMono.range_inj_of_wellFoundedLT), so I = I'. Then I(π(k)) = I(π'(k)) for every k, and injectivity of I gives π(k) = π'(k); hence π = π'.
   (c) Φ is surjective: for j ∈ Inj let σ := Tuple.sort j ∈ Perm(Fin n). Then j∘σ is monotone (Tuple.monotone_sort) and injective (a composition of injective maps), hence strictly increasing (Monotone.strictMono_of_injective); so (j∘σ, σ⁻¹) ∈ A × Perm(Fin n) and Φ(j∘σ, σ⁻¹) = j∘σ∘σ⁻¹ = j.

5. (Conclusion.) Reindexing the double sum of step 1 along the bijection Φ (Finset.sum_bij) and using step 3 for each pair (I, π),
   Σ_{(I, π) ∈ A × Perm(Fin n)} α(e∘I)² = Σ_{(I, π)} α(e∘(I∘π))² = Σ_{j ∈ Inj} α(e∘j)².
   By step 2 the right-hand side equals Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(e∘j)², and by step 1 the left-hand side equals n!·|α|_E². Hence Σ_{j : Fin n → Fin P} α(e∘j)² = n!·(covectorEuclideanNorm α)². ∎

Degenerate cases are covered by the same argument: for n = 0 the unique (empty) tuple is injective and strictly increasing, Perm(Fin 0) has one element and 0! = 1; for n > P (including P = 0 < n) no tuple j : Fin n → Fin P is injective and none is strictly increasing, so by step 2 every summand on the left vanishes, while N = 0 and the right-hand side is n!·(√0)² = 0.
proof_key_steps: |α|_E² = Σ_I [I strictly increasing] α(e∘I)² (Real.sq_sqrt), hence n!·|α|_E² = Σ_{(I, π) ∈ A × Perm(Fin n)} α(e∘I)².
Non-injective j make e∘j non-injective, so α(e∘j) = 0 and only injective tuples contribute.
(I, π) ↦ I∘π is a bijection from A × Perm(Fin n) onto the injective tuples (equal ranges force I = I'; Tuple.sort gives surjectivity).
Reindex along the bijection: Σ_j α(e∘j)² = n!·|α|_E².
